entries.mem0ai/mem0: Mem0 is a universal memory layer for AI agents and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, available as managed cloud or Apache-2.0 self-hosted open source. It supports semantic, keyword, and entity-based retrieval, with SDKs, a CLI, a self-hosted server, and a cloud platform.
entries.vectorize-io/hindsight: Hindsight provides long-term agent memory through retain, recall, and reflect operations. It offers Python, Node.js/TypeScript, and Go clients, and supports multiple LLM providers, including local options.
entries.volcengine/OpenViking: OpenViking is an open-source context database and official Hermes Agent memory provider that stores knowledge, memories, and skills in one virtual filesystem. Its directory-scoped search and L0 abstract, L1 overview, and L2 detail loading make it a fit for agents that need tiered context retrieval.
entries.topoteretes/cognee: Cognee is an open-source memory platform that builds connected memory from documents, code, and conversations. It supports local text processing without an LLM and includes a CLI for remembering and recalling text.
entries.supermemoryai/supermemory: Supermemory is a memory engine and API, as well as an official Hermes Agent memory provider, that extracts facts and handles updates, contradictions, and forgetting. It also offers connectors for services including Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive, and GitHub, alongside plugins, an MCP server, and JavaScript and Python API clients.
entries.garrytan/gbrain: Gbrain is an opinionated brain for OpenClaw and Hermes Agent that stores sourced facts and supports corrections and withdrawal. It can share memory across agents, with semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment available as options.
entries.plastic-labs/honcho: Honcho is a memory library for building stateful agents and the upstream library used by the elkimek/honcho-self-hosted Hermes wrapper. It stores messages and events on sessions and reasons in the background to update peer representations, with managed, local CLI, and self-hosted FastAPI options.
entries.campfirein/byterover-cli: ByteRover CLI treats memory as a Git repo, using Git-like version control to manage a context tree. It offers an interactive React/Ink TUI and REPL, supports 20 LLM providers, and includes 24 built-in agent tools.
entries.mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne: Mnemosyne is a SQLite-backed memory layer for Hermes agents with one pure-Python dependency. It integrates through MCP, native providers, or a Python SDK; its README reports BEAM results for v3.0.0 and says LongMemEval is pending.
entries.moorcheh-ai/memanto: Memanto consolidates memories and reconciles conflicting information, then briefs agents with relevant memories before they act. It also supports importing and exporting through the Open Knowledge Format.
entries.ClaudioDrews/memory-os: Memory OS is a seven-layer memory system for Hermes Agent that includes vector search and structured facts. It describes local infrastructure using Docker, Qdrant, Redis, and SQLite, and a Ground Truth hierarchy for prioritizing injected context.
entries.greyhaven-ai/autocontext: AutoContext is a recursive self-improving context harness for helping agents succeed on complex tasks. It runs tasks against evaluation, keeps useful lessons while discarding dead ends, and produces traces, reports, and playbooks.
entries.stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm: This Hermes Agent plugin uses a SQLite store and hierarchical DAG to persist messages, with the goal of never losing a message. Its lcm_grep and lcm_recall tools help recover details from stored context.
entries.vshulcz/deja-vu: deja-vu indexes past sessions from 42 supported agents so you can search them by text, agent, date, or project. It runs locally without models, embeddings, or a server, making it distinct from systems that generate or retrieve semantic memory.
entries.elkimek/honcho-self-hosted: This project provides a self-hosted Honcho backend for private, cross-session memory in Hermes Agent. It supports OpenAI-compatible providers and local inference servers, with an automated setup script for Docker, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
entries.Signet-AI/signetai: Signet provides a local-first layer for agent identity, memory, and secrets, with portable state across several agent harnesses and MCP clients. It can import files, webpages, and agent conversations, and includes a dashboard for browsing memory and sources.
entries.plur-ai/plur: plur stores shared agent memory as plain-text YAML engrams on disk and offers local search after a one-time model download, with keyword fallback. Its README reports 95.6% R@5 on LongMemEval-S (N=500).
entries.yoloshii/ClawMem: ClawMem is an on-device memory and context engine that combines BM25, vector search, rank fusion, and cross-encoder reranking. It can generate session handoffs and capture decisions and preferences, integrating through hooks, MCP, and native agent plugins.
entries.Sibyl-Labs/Sibyl-Memory: Sibyl-Memory keeps durable agent memory in a local SQLite file, with FTS5 search and a five-tier schema. Its package family includes an SDK, CLI, Hermes adapter, MCP server, and LangGraph BaseStore, without a vector database or embeddings.
entries.EfficientContext/ContextPilot: ContextPilot optimizes context ordering for prefix-cache sharing, including text and multimodal contexts. It provides a context index for reordering, deduplication, and cache-aware scheduling, and integrates with Hermes Agent, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, and OpenClaw.
entries.yantrikos/yantrikdb-hermes-plugin: This Hermes memory plugin provides explainable retrieval: each recall result includes a why_retrieved reason. It uses an embedded backend by default, with an HTTP option, and includes contradiction tracking and memory canonicalization.
entries.JanYork/llm-wiki-cli: llm-wiki-cli is an agent-driven memory tool that maintains a source-grounded Wiki with citations and history across sessions. It requires neither embeddings nor a vector database.
entries.ccf/agentcairn: agentcairn stores long-term, cross-project memory as inspectable Markdown files with frontmatter metadata, using an Obsidian vault as the source of truth. It adds a local DuckDB cache for hybrid search and retrieval, and connects to coding agents through MCP servers and host-specific plugins.
entries.amanning3390/flowstate-qmd: flowstate-qmd is a local-first memory project that uses SQLite-vec and GGUF models via node-llama-cpp. Its anticipatory cache watches agent session logs to prefetch context, and it provides an MCP-native server with automated configuration for major coding agent clients.
entries.yepyhun/Brainstack: Brainstack combines Hindsight, Graphiti, and MemPalace under a single memory owner, using SQLite, Kuzu, and Chroma for state and retrieval management. It provides the agent with a purpose-built evidence packet for each query.
entries.generalbusiness-ai/keep: Keep builds reflective memory with semantic search, BM25 full-text search, and ranked graph traversal. It can index codebases, URLs, and multimedia with OCR support, while edge tags connect notes through navigable, bidirectional relationships.
entries.aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer: Hermes Tool Slimmer reduces tool-schema token use with local keyword-based ranking and Tool Search support. It integrates through middleware without patching Hermes core on version 0.19 or later, and includes a dashboard for monitoring savings and managing configurations.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-context-os: Agent Context OS provides Git-backed context and workflows in plain Markdown for Claude Code, Codex, and compatible coding agents. Its first-class adapters support multiple agents, while reviewed handoffs use hash-checked proposals and receipts.
entries.Ladybug-Memory/hermes-memory-plugin: This local-only Hermes plugin stores memory in a single .lbdb embedded graph database file and uses importance-weighted recall to surface higher-priority entries during context prefetch. Retrieval supports BM25 keyword search and named graph relationships between entries.
entries.stepanov1975/hermes-local-knowledge: Hermes Local Knowledge indexes configured local sources and selected Hermes runtime sources for capability search and routing. It registers five tools for search, retrieval, traversal, feedback, and usage reports, along with session and pre-LLM-call hooks.
entries.MukundaKatta/hermes-agentmemory: Hermes AgentMemory uses on-demand summarization for pull-model episodic recall and supports immediate deletion of events. Its trace.jsonl file records prefetch operations for auditing.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/hermes-blind: Hermes Blind extracts the original goal from the first user turn of a long Claude Code or Codex session, with goals, first-sentence, and full extraction modes. It skips tool output and other non-user-turn records, and does not use a summarizing model or external service.
entries.piprail/piprail: Piprail provides a TypeScript SDK for x402 payments and an MCP server for budget-bound agent wallets. It operates without a backend, database, or API keys.
entries.yonro/hermes-xmemo-plugin: The XMemo plugin adds durable cross-session memory to Hermes Agent, using lifecycle hooks for pre-turn recall and session-end snapshots. It uses local SQLite caching and a write outbox, and can read memories from other connected agents.
entries.futurebrowser/hermes-exabase-plugin: The Exabase plugin integrates Exabase M-1 for self-organizing long-term agent memory. It provides tools to search and manually store memories, with configurable query expansion and result reranking for retrieval.
entries.sourcevault-ai/sourcevault-code-tools: SourceVault Code Tools provides private local code memory for repositories, with semantic search, file reads, and grounded Q&A. Its slash commands cover search, context, and Q&A, and it supports Hermes CLI, Telegram, and Hermes Desktop, plus repository sync and indexed Git-history search commands.
entries.visorcraft/MongrelDB-Hermes: MongrelDB-Hermes provides long-term memory for Hermes Agent, with AES-256-GCM encryption at rest enabled by default. It supports native Rust FFI or HTTP daemon execution and combines HNSW ANN, sparse, and FM-index retrieval.
entries.penfieldlabs/hermes-penfield: Penfield provides memory-management and knowledge-graph traversal tools for Hermes Agent. Its 17 tools include hybrid BM25, vector, and graph search, plus automatic context checkpointing during message compression.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-memory-kit: Agent Memory Kit is a file-based memory-curation loop that works with Markdown files and produces reviewable JSON diffs, without a database. Its rot and lint curators flag stale or conflicting facts, while a local Git repository tracks and can revert changes.

entries.obra/superpowers: Superpowers provides composable skills with instructions designed to make agents use them, plus a software-development workflow that moves from specification and design sign-off through planning and subagent execution. It belongs in a skills list for teams seeking a defined development methodology, with installation documented separately for multiple harnesses.
entries.nexu-io/open-design: Open Design is a local-first design and prototyping system that brings together skills, design templates, design systems, and plugins. Its support for multiple coding agents—including Hermes Agent—through skills, CLI, MCP, or runtime adapters makes it a design-focused option in this list.
entries.mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills: This repository offers structured cybersecurity skills across security domains, with mappings to frameworks including MITRE ATT&CK, ATLAS, D3FEND, and F3. Its breadth and compatibility with more than 26 AI platforms make it a framework-oriented choice for security work.
entries.Agents365-ai/drawio-skill: Drawio-skill turns natural-language prompts and real sources into editable .drawio diagrams. Incremental sync preserves manual layout and annotations, while the diagramctl CLI and optional MCP server provide ways to use it.
entries.internet-court/internet-court-skill: Internet Court combines a master router and connector skills with vendored copies of official protocol skills. It adds verification and dispute resolution, setting it apart as a skill for agent-to-agent commerce workflows.
entries.conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing: Avoid AI Writing can detect patterns, rewrite text, or edit prose in place, with optional casual, professional, technical, warm, and blunt profiles. Its command-line detector also works with files and piped text, making it a focused writing and editing skill.
entries.AMAP-ML/SkillClaw: SkillClaw uses background evolution to deduplicate skills and improve their quality, and unifies skill libraries across agents, devices, and team members. Its integrations include Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenAI-compatible APIs.
entries.wondelai/skills: This cross-platform library includes 51 expert frameworks and 14 guided metaskills for Claude Code, Codex, and agents compatible with agent-plugins.org specifications. It also maintains session state in the project's docs folder.
entries.mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills: This collection provides professional agent skills as plain Markdown files, with README-listed tasks such as writing PRDs and decoding leases. An installer copies the skill text files, and uninstalling removes them.
entries.ZeroPointRepo/youtube-skills: YouTube-skills covers transcripts, video search, channel browsing, and playlist extraction for Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Claude Code, and Cursor. Use requires a TranscriptAPI key, which has a 100-credit free tier.
entries.Romanescu11/hermes-skill-factory: Hermes Skill Factory watches active workflows for reusable patterns and can generate both SKILL.md documentation and Python plugin scaffolds. Slash commands let users manage, list, and save detected patterns.
entries.Cranot/super-hermes: Super-Hermes generates custom thinking instructions for specific tasks and includes pre-built analytical lenses for different domains. It reports findings alongside potential blind spots in the analysis.
entries.DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills: Adds type-safe agentskills.io support for Pydantic AI, including remote skill registries sourced from Git and S3. It also provides tools for bundled resources and script execution, with sandboxing to isolate untrusted scripts from the host.
entries.AkoliteZA/hermes-agent-idea-workflow: Turns rough ideas into structured design documents and implementation handoffs for Hermes Agent. Lite and Full modes accommodate different project complexity, and a review gate evaluates specs with PASS/FAIL models.
entries.tlehman/litprog-skill: Creates .lit.md documents that weave prose, diagrams, and source code, then extracts runnable files from them with a tangler. It also syncs source-file edits back into the literate document, making it suited to workflows where code and documentation evolve together.
entries.ReinaMacCredy/maestro: Provides a harness for long-running AI agents, with SQLite storage and event logging through a mechanism kernel. It coordinates agent teams using the SLP cooperative-agent protocol and distributes prompt-first working methods as Markdown recipes and skills.
entries.esaradev/icarus-plugin: Shares memory across instances through Markdown files and automatically captures high-value decisions and outcomes. It also includes a pipeline for fine-tuning and switching to replacement models.
entries.Hermes-brasil/hermes-brasil: Supports the Brazilian Hermes Agent community with Portuguese-language skills in SKILL.md format and guides for installation, configuration, and use. The project also describes contributions through forks and pull requests.
entries.black-forest-labs/skills: Provides prompting guidance for FLUX image and video generation alongside BFL API integration for polling and webhooks. Its FLUX 3 video suite includes eight specialist skills.
entries.smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills: Lists nine Chainlink skills that follow the Agent Skills spec and can be installed with `npx skills add smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills`. The README describes the repository as containing community examples only.
entries.armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge: Creates agent instructions from repositories, documentation, and developer discourse, with both automated and step-by-step workflows. It also supports skill testing and export.
entries.supernovae-st/nika: Nika describes itself as a workflow language for AI with one file, four verbs, and one Rust binary. It checks workflows before calling a model, runs with a model of your choice, and verifies each run’s tamper-evident record.
entries.chigwell/skilldock.io: Provides a registry of reusable AI skills based on the AgentSkills specification, with a Python client and CLI. Its installation process resolves dependencies recursively, and it includes commerce features using TON payments.
entries.tiann/execplan-skill: Supports autonomous execution of long-running, multi-step tasks with real-time tracking of progress and decisions. Built-in checkpoints and rollback procedures provide a path to recover from problems.
entries.adnw-vinc/hermes-nextcloud: This Hermes Agent skill manages Nextcloud files, notes, calendars, tasks, and contacts through WebDAV and CalDAV. It uses HTTPS with Nextcloud App Passwords and includes a guided setup script for validating credentials and configuring access.
entries.amanning3390/hermeshub: HermesHub is a community hub for browsing, searching, and installing skills, with federated search across GitHub and Hugging Face. It implements the Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) v0.9 specification and runs continuously via Hermes Agent on NVIDIA infrastructure.
entries.willingning-coder/eagle-eye: Eagle Eye narrows the skills presented before LLM calls using five retrieval layers, including hard triggers, full-text search, synonyms, and semantic embeddings. It can degrade gracefully when embedding models or dependencies are unavailable.
entries.EntangledQuantum/Life_OS: Life_OS is an ADHD-friendly personal execution system for habits and study blocks, with agent-driven scheduling and system design through an MCP connection. It stores data in a single local SQLite file and includes a React web app and an Expo-based Android application.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermaguard: Hermaguard performs read-only adversarial code review, using parallel subagents to examine edge cases, integrations, and other potential issues. It combines deterministic scans with proof-of-concept execution in a hardened sandbox to verify findings.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermes-simplify-swarm: This skill simplifies code with three parallel agents focused on Hygiene, Clarity, and Correctness. It supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, and Rust, and uses a tiered application process with an approval gate.
entries.teixeirazeus/fablize-for-hermes: Fablize for Hermes adapts verified procedures for breaking tasks into multiple stories, with mandatory evidence-based verification gates. It also provides an investigation protocol for reproduction and causal debugging, plus a Python goal engine for persistent task state.
entries.handnewb/hermes-cybersec-lab: This project provides a cybersecurity lab for Hermes Agent, with skills and tools for network, forensics, and exploitation work. Its highlights include more than 2,077 skills across repositories, 131+ tools, and integrations with 28 cybersecurity frameworks and standards.
entries.PederHP/skillsdotnet: Skillsdotnet implements agentskills.io in C# and .NET, using SKILL.md files for progressive disclosure. It integrates with Microsoft.Extensions.AI for tool-based skill loading and can automatically register common agent skill directories.
entries.Diabloluo/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is a local, read-only observability dashboard that tracks token costs, session history, and skill analytics in real time. It applies local log desensitization and offers optional incident alerts through Telegram and Feishu.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skills: This collection provides plain-markdown agent skills for code review and session management, including multi-session reconciliation and worktree recovery. Skills can be installed by copying a directory or using the bundled installer.
entries.conorbronsdon/demo-gif-skill: This Claude Code skill creates reproducible demo GIFs for repository READMEs, generating either VHS tape files or Playwright recording scripts. It supports terminal CLIs, TUIs, web apps, and libraries, and optimizes GIFs to target sizes under 8 MB.
entries.aidevelopers2/remoteopenclaw-mcp: This CLI and MCP server searches more than 13,870 MCP servers and 4,384 agent skills, then provides direct installation commands for discovered tools and plugins. Its support for MCP-compatible clients including Hermes makes it a discovery tool for agents in this list.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skill-builder: This project builds Claude Code extensions and portable Agent Skills core files, then validates them against runtime-specific profiles with CI-friendly exit codes. It also monitors official frontmatter specifications weekly to detect field changes.
entries.Carlo1911/skill-evolution: This host-agnostic feedback loop analyzes session history to identify skill coverage gaps and draft improvement proposals. Updates are gated by deterministic, LLM-judge, and regression evaluators, and the project runs locally using Python’s standard library without daemons or external services.
entries.CorsenAI/hermes-windows-runtime-skills: These Hermes Agent skills route file operations using path syntax suited to native Windows, Git Bash/MSYS, or WSL. They also select and verify existing project-compatible Python interpreters without installing one.
entries.superagnt/leverage: Leverage provides agent skills for social data, CRM management, and lead enrichment, with support for Claude Code, Cursor, and other agentskills.io-compliant clients. It also includes an MCP server for browser-based OAuth authentication.
entries.jiawood2006/hermes-skills: This collection includes skills to transcribe Douyin videos into structured Markdown and SRT subtitles, remove common Chinese AI-writing patterns with a rule-based engine, and extract structured data from PDFs and images using macOS Vision. It brings video, text, and document workflows together for Hermes Agent.
entries.webmilmind1/hermes-bounty-board: This Hermes Agent plugin lets agents browse open support bounties, purchase ticket context, and submit answers for human review; public wallet earnings records are available. Users can also create a bounty board, which returns a URL, API key, and USDC deposit addresses.
entries.mag3nt-com/openclaw-skill: This skill automates USDC payments for HTTP 402 responses and supports Pay Link, x402, MPP, and AP2 protocols. It is compatible with OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and the agentskills.io standard.
entries.skillseal/skillseal: Skillseal tests AI agent skills for structure, functionality, and security in isolated Docker containers. It produces Ed25519-signed certificates and provides a public API for certificate verification and skill submission.
entries.scavio-ai/hermes-agent: Scavio for Hermes Agent provides structured web data across 31 platforms through a hosted MCP server that exposes 191 tools. The project also includes five workflow skills and supports Claude, Cursor, Goose, and OpenHands.
entries.Shine8592/china-briefing: This Hermes Agent skill generates structured Chinese news briefings at geographic scales ranging from global to street level. Reports include core conclusions and action suggestions, and semantic memory uses user interests to expand searches.
entries.aidatatools-dev/astro-agents-mcp: This MCP server provides deterministic Western and Vedic astrology results using JPL DE440, with no LLM involved and SHA-256 hashes for verification. Its no-auth MCP endpoint and per-call x402 or MPP payments make it a distinct agent skill for astrology queries.
entries.parkyucheol-del/alphapipeline: This remote MCP offers token-risk checks and prediction-market slippage data for AI agents. MCP discovery and two onboarding tools are free, while most other tool calls require x402 payment.
entries.cablate/Agentic-MCP-Skill: A progressive MCP client that uses three-layer lazy loading to minimize token usage, with server metadata and tool schemas discovered incrementally. Its socket-based daemon architecture supports persistent connections, making it a distinct option for Hermes agents that need MCP access.

entries.numtide/llm-agents.nix: This project packages AI coding agents and development tools for Nix, including Hermes. Its packages are automatically updated daily, and the README lists Nix run commands for the available tools.
entries.marshallrichards/ClawPhone: ClawPhone provides scripts and notes for running agent CLIs, including Hermes Agent, on Android through Termux. Its highlights include an ARM64 Android installer for Antigravity CLI, OpenClaw configuration guides, and hardware and UI access through Termux:API and Termux:GUI.
entries.AbuZar-Ansarii/Hermes-Agent-On-Android: This Termux-based installer and guide runs Hermes Agent on Android using a proot-distro Ubuntu setup. It supports interactive model setup, gateway services, shell commands, and external providers or local models via Ollama.
entries.ultraworkers/hermes-agent-helm-chart: This unofficial community Helm chart deploys Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with single-writer state-safety guardrails for persistent HERMES_HOME storage. It offers direct deployment or operator-ready CRD workflows, plus configurable gateway mode with optional API and webhook listeners.
entries.amirghm/hermes-agent-mobile: This one-command installer brings the Hermes AI assistant to Android through Termux and to iOS through iSH. It also supports Telegram voice and file messaging, and scheduled tasks via cron jobs on Termux.
entries.TheAiSingularity/hermesclaw: hermesclaw runs Hermes Agent in a sandbox with hardware-enforced controls through NVIDIA OpenShell. It restricts network and filesystem access at the kernel level and provides configurable security policies for messaging and web search.
entries.solomon2773/nora: Nora is a self-hosted control plane for deploying, monitoring, and operating OpenClaw and Hermes agents on Docker or Kubernetes, with REST, CLI, and MCP interfaces. Its listed features include a 69-entry credential catalog, 17+ LLM provider integrations, and AES-256-GCM secret encryption with mandatory encryption keys.
entries.xmbshwll/hermes-agent-docker: This project provides a Docker sandbox image for Hermes Agent that includes mini-swe-agent and the official Hermes installation. It supports persistent state through mounted home directories and building specific Hermes tags with build arguments.
entries.0xrsydn/nix-hermes-agent: This Nix package and NixOS module supports reproducible Hermes deployment with declarative configuration for cli-config.yaml and workspace documents. It combines Nix-managed and CLI-installed skill management, and supports secrets integration through systemd EnvironmentFiles and sops-nix.
entries.jpalmae/hermeshq: HermesHQ is a Docker-first control plane for operating multiple Hermes Agent instances from one web application, with separate workspaces and identities for each. It provides per-agent Telegram and WhatsApp channels and granular tool, path, and network permission policies.
entries.MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG: Hermes OTG is a portable Hermes Agent package that runs from a USB or other drive without host installation or registry writes. It includes Desktop, TUI, and Gateway modes with isolated data environments, and bundles Python 3.12, PortableGit, and Sysinternals rescue tools for offline use.
entries.JackTheGit/hermes-autonomous-server: This project sets up Hermes Gateway as a headless, reboot-safe systemd service on Ubuntu and Debian servers, with Nous Portal integration. It also supports autonomous execution of recurring AI cron jobs.

entries.TauricResearch/TradingAgents: TradingAgents applies a multi-agent framework to financial trading: fundamental analysts assess company financials and performance metrics, while sentiment analysts aggregate news headlines, StockTwits, and Reddit chatter. Selected analysts work in parallel using their own tools, bringing different kinds of analysis to the trading process.
entries.builderz-labs/mission-control: Mission Control provides a self-hosted interface for governing agent registration, task dispatch, memory browsing, and cost tracking. It supports multi-agent workflows through a Web UI, CLI, MCP server, and REST API, with local Node.js installation or Docker deployment.
entries.agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires: Agent of Empires is a TUI and web control surface for managing multiple coding agents, including Hermes Agent and other named agent tools. It keeps sessions running in the background with tmux and offers sandboxing plus dashboards with diff review.
entries.shannhk/hermes-agent-control-room: This Control Room-first template describes a path from a single Hermes Agent on one VPS to specialist teams and automated workflows. Its level-based architecture uses a task bus for orchestrator-to-specialist delegation and handoffs, and includes skills for VPS provisioning, security auditing, and backup management.
entries.swarmclawai/swarmclaw: SwarmClaw is for building autonomous agent swarms, with support for 23+ LLM providers, durable agent memory, and MCP tool integration. Visual org charts show how agent teams are delegated, setting it apart as a swarm-oriented option.
entries.agent37-platform/minions: Minions offers a single-screen mission control for creating, supervising, and reviewing autonomous Hermes Agent work. Its Kanban board tracks task status and review queues, while live streams show agent reasoning and tool execution; proposed task completions require human verification.
entries.1ilkhamov/opencode-hermes-multiagent: This project coordinates 17 specialized agents across research, planning, implementation, quality, and infrastructure. A strict pipeline architecture and Master Orchestrator handle routing and coordination.
entries.linke-ai/hermes-agent-team: Hermes Agent Team is a local web system for collaboration between Leader and Specialist agents, managing an automated task lifecycle. It uses MCP and ACP for local tool and communication handling, with a real-time web UI for agent dialogues and Kanban task flows.
entries.howdymary/hermes-agent-metaharness: Hermes Agent Metaharness automates outer-loop optimization of benchmark harness code. It runs TBLite and TerminalBench-2 evaluations and provides structured candidate mutation and frontier tracking.
entries.runtimenoteslabs/gladiator: Gladiator stages two competing AI companies, orchestrating nine autonomous agents using Paperclip and Hermes Agent for task execution and learning. A real-time dashboard displays agent tasks, code, and scoreboard metrics.
entries.InfiniteWhispers/HermesAgent-MultiModel: HermesAgent-MultiModel implements a local Mixture-of-Agents stack by querying models in parallel and synthesizing their outputs, using Hermes for task routing and tool-calling. It is designed for consumer GPUs, with stated optimization for RTX 4080/5080 hardware and no cloud dependencies.

entries.colbymchenry/codegraph: Codegraph builds a full project graph with `codegraph init`, using structural extraction and cross-file resolution across supported languages. Its MCP support makes that pre-indexed code knowledge available to Hermes Agent and other coding agents.
entries.junhoyeo/tokscale: Tokscale tracks token usage and costs across Hermes and a range of other coding-agent clients. It offers both a CLI and a visualization dashboard for reviewing that usage.
entries.liaohch3/claude-tap: Claude Tap records coding-agent API traffic and provides a self-contained HTML viewer for exported trace sessions. It supports clients including Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Cursor CLI, and redacts common authentication headers before recording.
entries.Javis603/token-monitor: Token Monitor is a real-time widget for token usage, costs, and rate limits across 46+ AI coding tools, including Hermes Agent. It also shows historical trends and usage breakdowns, with multi-device sync.
entries.bergside/typeui: TypeUI provides design systems and layout guidance through MCP servers to help build UI with AI. It works with Hermes Agent and other listed tools, and is compatible with AI providers that support markdown or general prompting.
entries.Salomondiei08/oh-my-hermes: Oh My Hermes adds an opinionated workflow layer for building, shipping, and operating apps with Hermes Agent. Its skills cover product briefs, design handoffs, and implementation, while seven agents span product-lifecycle roles; GitHub integration can enable issue and pull request delivery.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-skins: Hermes Skins is a community CLI for customizing the Hermes terminal UI with banner colors, spinners, and ASCII art. YAML-based configuration supports theme creation, with examples including retro DOS and cyberpunk styles.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/lintlang: Lintlang is a command-line static linter for AI agent configurations, tool descriptions, and system prompts, using HERM v1.1 scoring. It scans prompts, tool definitions, schemas, and agent files, then reports findings with specific fixes and supported line references.
entries.tinyhumansai/tiny.place: Tiny.place describes itself as a social economy for autonomous AI agents. It supports encrypted agent-to-agent messaging via Signal Protocol, identity registration with human-readable @handles, and commerce through Solana-based USDC and SOL payments.
entries.unmodeled-tyler/vessel-browser: Vessel Browser is an AI-native browser built for autonomous agent control via MCP. It supports external MCP clients and browser automation workflows, and includes a supervisor sidebar for agent approvals, checkpoints, and conversation threads.
entries.AlexAI-MCP/hermes-CCC: Hermes-CCC ports the Hermes Agent brain and 46 core skills to Claude Code Channel, where it runs without separate processes or OAuth. It also includes MLOps tools for vLLM, GGUF inference, and RL training.
entries.topoteretes/cognee-integrations: Cognee Integrations is a monorepo of Cognee-owned integration packages, organized into permanent knowledge graph and session cache tiers. Its Claude Code plugin can automatically capture and recall context.
entries.adityahimaone/hermes-agent-rtk-caveman: This setup combines RTK and Caveman templating in CLI workflows that it says can save 90–99% of tokens. It also includes 40+ preconfigured skills for finance, DevOps, and research, with automated installation for macOS and Linux.
entries.Abruptive/Ankh.md: Ankh.md is a framework for creating scoped Hermes Agents with per-folder configuration and skills. It supports switching between default and scoped agents, with project-local memories, tools, and custom instructions.
entries.42-evey/evey-setup: This project automates installation of Hermes Agent and 12+ supporting services, with three deployment tiers ranging from a minimum viable setup to a production stack. It also supports 29 community plugins across six functional categories.
entries.0xNyk/openclaw-to-hermes: This migration tool moves OpenClaw data—including SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, skills, and memory archives—to Hermes. It also maps configurations and credentials to Hermes YAML and JSON formats and sets up systemd gateway services.
entries.observeco/observeco: Observeco monitors multi-agent systems through a native Hermes plugin that exports real-time conversation telemetry. Its two monitoring modes include passive analysis and scheduled active probing, while config-aware baselines help detect performance drift relative to local file changes.
entries.handnewb/hermes-voice: Hermes Voice adds voice interaction with wake-word support and offline operation without API keys or accounts. It supports 35 languages via Piper and 9 via Kokoro, along with adaptive turn-taking and barge-in.
entries.33hodl/hermes-startup: Hermes Startup provides a local runtime that operates deterministically with zero network access by default. It requires explicit approval for consequential actions and external writes, and includes contracts for opportunities, offer previews, and exact approvals.
entries.181079342/hermes-memoss: This Hermes memory plugin provides semantic search and multi-dimensional memory storage. It includes tools to search, add, and delete memories, plus a circuit breaker for MemOS API outages.

entries.farion1231/cc-switch: CC Switch is a cross-platform manager for Hermes Agent and several other agent CLIs, including Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI. It lets users switch API providers in one click and manage MCP, Skills, and Prompts on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
entries.iOfficeAI/AionUi: AionUi is a local open-source cowork app for Hermes Agent and other agent CLIs. It includes a built-in agent with file access, web search, and MCP tools, plus 21 ready-to-use assistants, and runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
entries.nesquena/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI lets users work with Hermes Agent from a web browser or phone, with sessions, chat, and workspace files arranged in a three-panel layout. Its file browser includes inline previews, and the project uses Python and vanilla JavaScript with no build step.
entries.fathah/hermes-desktop: Hermes Desktop is a desktop companion for installing, configuring, and chatting with Hermes Agent, using the official Hermes install script. Its GUI manages profiles, sessions, skills, and tools, and the app is available from the project website or GitHub Releases.
entries.EKKOLearnAI/ekko-studio: Ekko Studio is a Hermes Agent web dashboard for chat, session management, scheduled jobs, usage analytics, and channel configuration. It also offers shared and group chats, visual workflows, persistent sessions, and tools for files, voice, devices, and agent management; it is available as a desktop app for Windows, macOS, and Linux, as well as through npm and Docker.
entries.outsourc-e/hermes-workspace: Hermes Workspace brings chat, a terminal, a memory browser, a skills manager, and an inspector panel into a web workspace. It also includes Swarm Mode with role-based dispatch and tmux-backed workers, plus a file browser with Monaco and a PTY terminal.
entries.spacering-net/codeg: Codeg is a collaborative multi-agent coding workspace that gathers sessions from Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and other agents in a desktop or self-hosted app. Users can import, search, resume, and hand off sessions, or delegate with @ and queue to-dos in worktrees; the workspace includes 15 built-in agents, and ACP agents can also join.
entries.dodo-reach/hermes-desktop: This native Mac workspace connects directly to Hermes hosts locally or over SSH and provides views for sessions, Kanban, skills, and cron jobs. Its embedded terminal gives users direct shell access for tasks such as system repair.
entries.Eynzof/Hermes-CN-Desktop: Hermes-CN-Desktop is a Windows-first desktop app for Hermes Agent, built with Tauri, TypeScript, and Rust, with support for Windows and macOS. It includes a Hermes-CN-Core kernel with health checks and updates, alongside interfaces for chat, memory management, and LaTeX and Markdown rendering.
entries.abundantbeing/hermes-browser-extension: This Chromium side-panel extension connects browser context to a local, cloud, or self-hosted remote Hermes gateway. Users can attach page context, files, or staged screenshots, and Chromium-only Hermes Control can operate tabs.
entries.uzairansaruzi/hermex: Hermex is a native SwiftUI app for iOS 18 and later that lets users drive a self-hosted Hermes agent from an iPhone by pairing with a hermes-webui server. It is a client only, so users run the server themselves; the app is free and has no analytics or tracking.
entries.freestylefly/wesight: Wesight is a desktop AI agent workspace with one-click setup for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw, alongside custom LLM model routing. It includes a runtime dashboard for token usage and latency, plus a live workspace for monitoring code writes and diffs.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-hud: This interactive TUI gives Hermes operators a nine-tab view of agent growth, Git projects, and scheduled cron jobs, with four selectable color themes. Its tmux operator view sets it apart by helping manage live agent panes.
entries.jazzyalex/agent-sessions: This native macOS app brings session browsing, search, analytics, and quota tracking together for Hermes agents and other coding-agent CLIs. It can search prompts, responses, tool activity, and errors, then resume supported sessions in Terminal.app, iTerm2, or Warp.
entries.xaspx/hermes-control-interface: This self-hosted web dashboard brings Hermes stack controls into a browser, including a terminal, file explorer, session overview, cron management, system metrics, and agent status. It also offers real-time chat with tool-call visualization, an MCP server control plane, and a ZOO Swarm Monitor for agent health and kanban pipelines.
entries.nickvasilescu/hermes-desktop-os1: This native macOS workspace runs Hermes Agent on Orgo cloud computers and SSH hosts, with one-click automated installation on fresh cloud computers. Its integrated WebRTC voice mode uses OpenAI Realtime and Orgo MCP.
entries.sharbelxyz/hermes-agent-mission-control: This self-hostable dashboard template connects a local Hermes agent to web dashboards through a Postgres message bus. Its approval inbox lets users review requests with side effects before they proceed.
entries.liftaris/herm: Built with OpenTUI, herm offers an alternative interface for chatting with Hermes Agent and managing sessions. It also combines a kanban board for agentic work with controls for profiles, skills, cron jobs, and toolsets.
entries.clawvader-tech/hermes-telegram-miniapp: This locally run, mobile-first React SPA provides a 10-page dashboard for Telegram Mini App v2.0. Its terminal chat supports streaming responses and file attachments, while background agent spawning supports up to five concurrent instances.
entries.aivrar/portable-hermes-agent: This project packages Hermes Agent as a portable Windows desktop application, with no installation, Docker, or admin rights required. Its highlights include 100 tools across more than 20 toolsets, cloud and LM Studio local models, and a workflow engine with scheduling, conditions, loops, and parallel execution.
entries.pyrate-llama/hermes-ui: This self-hosted Hermes assistant has a glassmorphic web interface for chat and real-time log streaming. A file browser, task tracking dashboard, and management tools for skills, cron jobs, and MCP servers round out the workspace.
entries.sanchomuzax/hermes-webui: This dashboard focuses on monitoring Hermes processes and configuration, with real-time session activity and cost tracking. It also allows full inspection of conversation histories and skill source code, alongside read-only views of configuration and environment variables.
entries.Euraika-Labs/pan-ui: This self-hosted, chat-first AI workspace combines real-time SSE streaming and tool approval cards with runtime controls. Its marketplace supports discovering and installing skills and MCP servers, while isolated profiles keep sessions, memory, and API keys separate.
entries.Felix-Forever/hermes-agent-desktop: This native desktop client supports collaboration among 20 specialized AI agents, with a PM orchestrator and streaming chat. Its visual Skill Store offers more than 50 curated one-click installations, alongside model switching.
